# Independent audit of minimal-active rank and projective row variation

Full source read: `candidate f62fe2e83b180bf3`.

**PASS.** The continuity proof applies even to a probability law with atoms. Its upper bound tests a fixed positive-probability threshold before taking an infimum, so no atom-crossing limit is presumed. Its lower bound uses the minimum of the strictly positive coordinates of the limiting row and correctly leaves zero coordinates unrestricted. Compactness then gives an attained weighted maximum and an integer minimum number of active rows.

Any linear dependence among nonzero nonnegative active rows has coefficients of both signs. The proposed row rescalings preserve all columns exactly, are feasible in both signs near zero, and make the homogeneous objective affine. A maximum makes that affine slope zero. A finite endpoint kills at least one row without creating any, proving independence for the chosen minimal-active maximizer.

The full-row variation funded by proportional rescalings of the active rows is exactly feasible and preserves existing zeros. The projective identity using s=t/(1+t a_r) is exact. After the forced vanishing of the total first variation, the objective remainder is precisely the one-row remainder multiplied by a positive scalar. Thus a positive second directional variation in the active-row span contradicts maximality without requiring any other row to be differentiable. The stated intersection dimension k+p>m is correct.

The final positive-curvature premise is substantive. `candidate 61582452a1450270` gives a full proper row with a negative-semidefinite Hessian and only radial kernel, so rank alone does not supply the missing positive direction. The source correctly states its curvature conclusions conditionally and makes no unproved all-row assertion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
